source_user: Advanced cluster case NVIDIA Dynamo-4: Design an evaluation of NVIDIA Dynamo for disaggregated inference orchestration. Variant 4 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: separate frontend routing, prefill workers, decode workers, KV movement, transport overhead, scheduling policy, queueing, model compatibility, observability, and failover behavior. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: Treat Dynamo as an architecture under test, not a guaranteed optimization. Fix the model/checkpoint, tokenizer, prompt/output and arrival distributions, batching, parallelism, GPU/NIC/NUMA topology, software versions, supported transport and routing policy. Define frontend routing, queue ownership, prefill/decode assignment, KV handoff, scheduling, compatibility and failover; also specify admission/backpressure, cancellation, retries, observability and model/version checks. Hypothesis: at matched workload and output quality, Dynamo improves throughput or TTFT/ITL tails versus local or conventional distributed serving without exceeding declared KV-transfer, queueing, error or recovery limits. Run randomized repeated paired trials across short and long contexts, burstiness and worker imbalance; measure TTFT, ITL p50/p95/p99, requests/tokens per second, queue depth and wait, prefill/decode utilization, batch sizes, KV bytes and transfer latency, rejects, errors and recovery time with units and sample counts. Kill frontend, prefill, decode and transport components, and verify bounded retries, no lost or duplicated requests, safe cancellation and compatibility rejection. Canary limited traffic and route to the known-good path on SLO, integrity or failover-gate failure; retain versioned configs, traces and raw samples.
